title: Sasha Circle
statementMd:
Berlanders like to eat cones after a hard day. Misha Square and Sasha Circle are local authorities of Berland. Each of them controls its points of cone trade. Misha has $*n*$ points, Sasha — $*m*$. Since their subordinates constantly had conflicts with each other, they decided to build a fence in the form of a circle, so that the points of trade of one businessman are strictly inside a circle, and points of the other one are strictly outside. It doesn't matter which of the two gentlemen will have his trade points inside the circle.

Determine whether they can build a fence or not.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10000)$, numbers of Misha's and Sasha's trade points respectively.

The next $*n*$ lines contains pairs of space-separated integers $*M*_{*x*}, *M*_{*y*}$ ($- 10^{4} ≤ *M*_{*x*}, *M*_{*y*} ≤ 10^{4}$), coordinates of Misha's trade points.

The next $*m*$ lines contains pairs of space-separated integers $*S*_{*x*}, *S*_{*y*}$ ($- 10^{4} ≤ *S*_{*x*}, *S*_{*y*} ≤ 10^{4}$), coordinates of Sasha's trade points.

It is guaranteed that all $*n* + *m*$ points are distinct.

## Output

The only output line should contain either word "`YES`" without quotes in case it is possible to build a such fence or word "`NO`" in the other case.

## Note

In the first sample there is no possibility to separate points, because any circle that contains both points $( - 1, 0), (1, 0)$ also contains at least one point from the set $(0,  - 1), (0, 1)$, and vice-versa: any circle that contains both points $(0,  - 1), (0, 1)$ also contains at least one point from the set $( - 1, 0), (1, 0)$

In the second sample one of the possible solution is shown below. Misha's points are marked with red colour and Sasha's are marked with blue. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5ca1c4797c22c929f81f0f0c0f3920142c7ba176.png)
statementZhMd:
伯兰人喜欢在辛苦的一天后吃甜筒。Misha Square 和 Sasha Circle 是伯兰的地方官员。他们各自管理着甜筒交易点。Misha 有 $*n*$ 个交易点，Sasha 有 $*m*$ 个交易点。由于他们的下属之间经常发生冲突，他们决定修建一道圆形围栏，使其中一位商人的所有交易点都严格位于圆内，而另一位商人的所有交易点都严格位于圆外。至于哪位商人的交易点位于圆内并不重要。

请判断他们能否修建这样的围栏。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 10000)$，分别表示 Misha 和 Sasha 的交易点数量。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行每行包含一对由空格分隔的整数 $*M*_{*x*}, *M*_{*y*}$ ($- 10^{4} ≤ *M*_{*x*}, *M*_{*y*} ≤ 10^{4}$)，表示 Misha 的交易点坐标。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行每行包含一对由空格分隔的整数 $*S*_{*x*}, *S*_{*y*}$ ($- 10^{4} ≤ *S*_{*x*}, *S*_{*y*} ≤ 10^{4}$)，表示 Sasha 的交易点坐标。

保证所有 $*n* + *m*$ 个点互不相同。

## 输出格式

输出一行：如果可以修建这样的围栏，输出不带引号的单词 `YES`；否则输出单词 `NO`。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，不存在分隔这些点的方法，因为任何同时包含点 $( - 1，0)$ 和 $(1，0)$ 的圆，至少还会包含集合 $(0， - 1)$、$(0，1)$ 中的一个点；反之，任何同时包含点 $(0， - 1)$ 和 $(0，1)$ 的圆，也至少会包含集合 $( - 1，0)$、$(1，0)$ 中的一个点。

在第二个样例中，下面展示了一种可行的方案。Misha 的点用红色标记，Sasha 的点用蓝色标记。![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5ca1c4797c22c929f81f0f0c0f3920142c7ba176.png)
